    To StartAnother-slice pepperoni pizza squaresA guard offers another slice at the end. Crisp tray pizza with pepperoni and mozzarella.How to make it400g pizza dough200g passata1 tsp dried oregano200g mozzarella, grated100g sliced pepperoni salami30g parmesan, finely grated2 tbsp olive oilOil a large baking tray and press the dough out to the edges.Spread with passata seasoned with the oregano and a pinch of salt.Scatter over the mozzarella and pepperoni, then the parmesan.Bake at 240°C until the base is crisp and the cheese is blistered.Cut into squares and serve hot.Fiji kokoda cups with coconut and limeTruman still dreams of getting to Fiji. Lime-cured fish in coconut cream with chilli.How to make it400g very fresh snapper fillets, diced4 limes200ml coconut cream1 small red chilli, finely chopped1 Lebanese cucumber, diced1 tomato, diced2 spring onions, sliced1 baby cos lettuce, leaves separatedToss the fish with the juice of 3 limes and a pinch of salt and chill until it turns white.Drain off most of the lime juice.Stir in the coconut cream, chilli, cucumber, tomato and spring onion.Spoon into the lettuce cups and finish with the last lime.Good morning blueberry muffinsAnd in case I don't see ya.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsMeryl's I-made-macaroni bakeMeryl made macaroni. Smoky ham macaroni under a gruyere crust.How to make it400g macaroni50g butter3 tbsp plain flour750ml milk1 tsp Dijon mustard150g vintage cheddar, grated100g gruyere, grated200g smoked ham, diced40g panko breadcrumbsBoil the macaroni until just short of tender and drain.Melt the butter, stir in the flour for a minute, then whisk in the milk until thick.Take off the heat and stir in the mustard, cheddar and half the gruyere.Fold through the pasta and ham and tip into a baking dish.Top with the rest of the gruyere and the panko and bake at 200°C until golden and bubbling.Painted-sky sailor's fish pieTruman sails into the painted sky. Snapper pie under buttery mash.How to make it500g skinless snapper fillets, in chunks250g raw prawns, peeled1 leek, sliced60g butter, plus 50g for the mash3 tbsp plain flour500ml milk2 tbsp chopped dill1 lemon, zested1kg floury potatoes100ml warm milk, for the mashBoil the potatoes until tender, then mash with 50g butter and the warm milk.Soften the leek in 60g butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk until thick.Stir in the fish, prawns, dill and lemon zest and tip into a baking dish.Spread over the mash, rough up the top with a fork and bake at 200°C until golden.Something SweetMount Nicaragua Mococoa potsMeryl pitches Mococoa in the middle of a fight. Rich cocoa custard under whipped cream.How to make it300ml thickened cream, plus 150ml for whipping200ml milk150g dark chocolate, chopped2 tbsp Dutch cocoa4 egg yolks60g caster sugar1 tsp vanilla extractHeat 300ml cream and the milk until steaming, then stir in the chocolate and cocoa until smooth.Whisk the yolks, sugar and vanilla, then whisk in the hot chocolate cream.Pour into 4 small cups in a deep tray, add hot water halfway up, and bake at 150°C until just set with a wobble.Chill, then top with the rest of the cream, softly whipped.To DrinkMarlon's now-that's-a-beer lagerMarlon holds the can right up to the camera. Ice-cold American lager in the can.How to make it4 x 355ml cans of American lager2 cups ice cubesChill the cans on ice until very cold.Hand them out with a straight face and the label facing the room.Cue the sun orange juiceChristof decides when morning starts.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
